---
title: "Sell a template"
description: "Pricing, payouts and what Rerun takes."
---

On Rerun Cloud, a template can be free, sold once, or sold monthly. You set the price and Rerun handles checkout, tax and the payout. A self-hosted install has no marketplace: every template there is free.

## Pricing models

Pick one on the **Pricing** tab of the template, in **My templates**.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Free" icon="gift">
    Anyone on a Rerun plan installs it. Good for building a reputation and feeding the directory.
  </Card>
  <Card title="One-time purchase" icon="tag">
    Charged once. The buyer keeps it for good.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Monthly subscription" icon="refresh-cw">
    Charged every month. Access ends when the buyer cancels, and the coworkers it installed switch off.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

A paid template starts at **\$5** and goes up to **\$2,000**. The price is in USD, excluding VAT: VAT is added on top at checkout and paid by the buyer, so it never comes out of your side.

Buyers still need an active Rerun plan to install a template, so a purchase unlocks the template and nothing else.

## What Rerun takes

**5% + \$0.30 per sale**, calculated on the amount net of tax. The rest is yours. The **Pricing** tab shows your price, the Rerun fee and what you earn before you save.

For a \$20 sale with no tax, that is \$1.30 to Rerun and \$18.70 to you.

A refund reverses the split: you give back your share, Rerun gives back its fee. A full refund also takes the template back from the buyer.

## Getting paid

Payouts go through Stripe Connect. Open the workspace menu, **Templates** > **My templates**, then **Payouts** under the list of your templates, and complete the Stripe onboarding once. Continuing means you accept the Marketplace Creator Terms.

The **Payouts** row carries the state of your Stripe account:

| State | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Not set up** | No Stripe account yet. **Set up payouts** starts the onboarding |
| **Action needed** | Stripe still needs a few details. **Finish setup** takes you back |
| **In review** | Stripe is verifying your details, usually a few minutes |
| **Restricted** | Stripe restricted the account. Your published templates stay online, but nobody can buy them until it is resolved |
| **Ready** | You can sell. **Open Stripe dashboard** opens your Stripe account |

Payouts follow Stripe's standard schedule.

<Warning>
  You cannot submit a paid template until your Stripe account can actually receive payouts. The submission checklist verifies it, so do the onboarding first. You can still save a price before that.
</Warning>

Payout onboarding needs a browser. It is the one part of the template workflow that is not available over the API.

## Tracking sales

**Revenue**, under **Payouts**, shows your sales over 30 days, 12 months or all time: the number of sales, the gross amount, the Rerun fee and what you earned. Below, your Stripe balance (**Pending payout** and **Available now**), your active subscriptions and what they bring each month, and the recent sales, each tied to the template that produced it.

## Pricing advice

- Price against the work it saves, not against the tokens it burns. The buyer pays for their own model usage on top.
- A monthly subscription fits a coworker that keeps earning its place: a monitor, a weekly report, an inbox triage. A one-time purchase fits a setup that is done once.
- Be honest about the setup time. A template that takes an hour to connect and says five gets refunded.
- The install script is part of the product. A template that configures itself well is worth more than one that leaves the buyer guessing.
- The price is set while the template is a draft. Once it is published, a price change goes through the Rerun team and only applies to new buyers.
